To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a platform for the high-throughput, dose dependent, temporal analysis of the effect of vitamins, minerals, TGFβ, and combinations thereof on chondrogenesis.

we have developed a high-throughput chondrogenesis analytic platform and used it to discover that the optimal continual supplement of copper, vitamin K, and TGF-β1 gives a 2.4 fold increase in COL2a1 promoter driven expression over TGF-β3 supplemented media alone in chondrogenic ATDC5 cells, which is a significant increase.
vitamins and minerals, in combination with TTFβ1, can enhance chondrogenic expression in a dose-dependent manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of vitamins, minerals, TGFβ1 on chondrogenesis in a high-throughput platform.
the effect of vitamins, minerals and TGFβ on COL2A 1 promoter-driven gene expression in ATDC5 chondrogenic cells.
the effect of vitamins/minerals and TGFβ on chondrogenesis, and how these effects are modulated by their interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the addition of copper, zinc, vitamin K, vitamin C, vitamin E, vitamin A, and vitamin D to chondrogenic cultures, either alone or in combination, has the ability to increase chondrogenic differentiation in vitro.

the addition of vitamins and minerals to chondrogenic medium in the presence of growth factors, such as TGFβ1 and BMP-2, can improve the expression of chondrogenic markers and increase the metabolic activity of chondrogenesis in vitro.
the optimal continual supplement of copper, vitamin K, and TGF-β1 gives a 2.8-fold increase in COLA2 promoter-driven expression over control (no TGF-β) supplemented media alone in chondrocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of vitamins and minerals in the presence of growth factors can significantly improve the quality of tissue engineered cartilage.
a high-throughput temporal and dose dependent, effect of vitamins and mineral on chondrogenesis was discovered.
a continual supply of copper, vitamin K, vitamin B6, and vitamin B12 is essential for chondrogenesis, and that the addition of TGFβ3 to the continual supplement is essential for chONDROGENESIS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vitamins and minerals have an effect on the expression of chondrogenic genes in a dose dependent, time dependent, and combinatorial fashion.
a high-throughput platform for chondrogenesis can identify combinatorial effects of vitamins and minerals in the presence of chondrogenic factors.
the use of a high-throughput platform can reveal significant combinatorial effects that can be missed by traditional methods.
